title: BOX OF VINTAGE PERIODICALS & E...
reason: Under-described box with a 1929 Keith Anderson (Kookaburra) memorial order of service, Sydney Harbour Bridge print and newspapers, and a bound Boer War periodical volume; likely $120-300 to ephemera and aviation collectors (my estimate).
findings: More than periodicals: the box holds Australian aviation and Sydney ephemera. (1) A printed 'In Memoriam' order of service card for Flight-Lieut. Keith Anderson (a line mentioning Royal Air Force is partly legible), Mosman Presbyterian Church, minister The Rev. D. P. Macdonald (ex-Chaplain A.I.F.), organist Dr Keith Barry (ex-Capt. 4th Dorsets, attached R.A.F.), dated '6th July 192?' (last digit unclear), 10.30 a.m., with a portrait photo. Keith Anderson was the Kookaburra pilot who died in the Tanami Desert in April 1929 while searching for Kingsford Smith; a web search snippet seen on 19/10/2026 put his burial at Mosman on 6 July 1929, which fits the card. (2) A newspaper clipping headed 'Maps and Radio. How News Will Come. Tracing the flight of a giant bird' with a pilot portrait (flight and date not confirmed). (3) A large colour print captioned 'The Sydney Harbour Bridge ... A Watercolour by J... A...' (artist name unreadable; the second line may refer to the bridge opening, March 1932, low confidence) and a large black and white print of a dense crowd with flags (caption illegible). (4) Three old Sydney newspapers: Sydney Morning Herald, Daily Telegraph and a masthead ending '...NING NEWS' (probably Evening News); dates not legible. (5) An open bound volume of a Boer War illustrated periodical (running head looks like 'BATTLE BOOK', low confidence) with a 'Soldiers' Letters' section and a photo page captioned 'Major Robin and Adjutant, New Zealand Contingent ... celebrated for his gallant ride of 1 1/2 miles under fire ('Spear.')'. (6) A LIFE International special double issue 'The World in Our Time: A Pictorial Atlas for the Space Age' and a furniture advertisement clipping (E. G. Glass, George Street). One web search found no sale record for the Anderson card, so its value is an estimate only.
condition: Typical aged paper: toned and browned newsprint, folds and creases, edge curling and small tears on the large prints, foxing on the bound volume; no missing pages seen on the open spread; LIFE issue looks fair.
rescore_note: Coherent c.1929 to 1932 Sydney ephemera: a Keith Anderson (Kookaburra) memorial order of service, Harbour Bridge prints, old Sydney papers and a bound Boer War periodical; real niche interest but no comps and paper dates unconfirmed, my estimate about $100 to $160 (search budget used up).
